Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.domain.conversation

Interface ConversationRepository

All Known Implementing Classes:
ConversationRepositoryAdapter
public interface ConversationRepository
Domain repository port for the Conversation aggregate and its child Message aggregate (design §4.1).

Pure Java — no Spring annotations. The adapter implementing this interface lives under infrastructure/persistence/adapter/ and bridges to Spring Data JPA (US-10-003).

int pageSize is used instead of the application-layer PageSize wrapper because the hexagonal layering rule forbids the domain from referencing the application layer; the application service unwraps PageSize.value() before calling the port — matching the existing AgentRepository / ApiKeyRepository convention.

Message operations live on this port (rather than a separate MessageRepository) because a Message is a child aggregate of Conversation addressed by (conversationId, messageId); same shape as AgentRepository carrying the team-membership operations.

    • save

    • findById

      Optional<Conversation> findById(ConversationId id)

    • listByOwner

      Page<Conversation> listByOwner(ConversationOwner owner, Optional<AgentId> agentFilter, Cursor cursor, int pageSize)
      Returns one page of conversations owned by owner, ordered newest-first ((createdAt, id) DESC), optionally narrowed to a single agent via agentFilter. The adapter switches exhaustively on the sealed ConversationOwner to dispatch the right where clause against the V005 XOR columns (owner_user_id / owner_client_id).

    • deleteById

      void deleteById(ConversationId id)
      Hard-deletes the conversation identified by id. Messages cascade via the V001 FK chain (messages.conversation_id … on delete cascade). A non-existent id is a silent no-op at this layer; the use case is responsible for surfacing 404.

    • appendMessage

      Message appendMessage(Message message)
      Appends a Message to its parent conversation. Does NOT bump the parent's MessageCount — the caller is responsible for performing the read-modify-write of Conversation.incrementMessageCount(java.time.OffsetDateTime) and save(Conversation) in the same transactional boundary (REQ-STR-002 persistence ordering).

    • listMessages

      Page<Message> listMessages(ConversationId conversationId, Cursor cursor, int pageSize)
      Returns one page of messages of conversationId in chronological ascending order ((createdAt, id) ASC) — opposite of the conversations list. Backs GET /conversations/{conversationId}/messages (US-10-010).

    • findLastN

      List<Message> findLastN(ConversationId conversationId, int n)
      Returns the last n messages of conversationId in chronological ascending order. Backs EPIC-11's memory-window assembly (REQ-AGT-005). Implementations SHOULD query in descending order with LIMIT n and reverse before returning, so the database can use the (conversation_id, created_at, id) index.
